top_stories.title: DeepSeek releases open-source Harness v0.1 coding framework
points: Harness v0.1 enters developer preview as an open-source alternative to paid AI coding agents like Claude Code (a terminal-based AI coding assistant).
Modular plugin architecture lets developers select, swap, or extend capabilities via configuration files without touching source code.
Every model interaction is written to an append-only session log for auditability (a record that can only be added to, never edited).
DeepSeek also shipped V4-Pro, a model tuned for agents, while raising API prices for existing V4 access.

unique_angles.point: Frames Harness as a direct free alternative to paid coding tools, arriving alongside imminent DeepSeek API price hikes.

top_stories.title: Zhipu/Z.ai GLM-5.3 claims coding-benchmark lead over OpenAI
points: GLM 5.3 beats OpenAI's Fable 5 and DeepSeek V4 on coding benchmarks, including Terminal Bench 2.1 (a test of agents completing real command-line tasks).
Gains came purely from scaled post-training (extra training after the base model is built) on the same 743B-parameter base as v5.2.
Available now via API; full open weights (downloadable model files) ship in roughly two weeks.
Zhipu says the model found 2,436 software vulnerabilities across decades-old open-source projects.

unique_angles.point: Highlights the 2,436-vulnerability discovery result as evidence of practical security capability.

items.title: OpenAI launches Ultrafast API tier and hits $40B run rate
points: Ultrafast tier runs GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 output tokens per second (tokens = word fragments the model generates), 14x the Standard tier, powered by Cerebras hardware.
Initially limited to select customers, aimed at real-time products where latency destroys usefulness.
Revenue run rate reached $40 billion in 2026, roughly double late 2025, driven by AI coding tools, subscriptions and a nascent ads business, ahead of a planned IPO.

items.title: X open-sources its ranking algorithm and shadowban checker
points: The 'For You' algorithm and core ranking engine released under Apache v2 license, said to be 10-15x more detailed than prior disclosures.
New tools let users see if and how ranking systems suppressed their account or posts, addressing 'shadowbanning' (invisible reduction of content reach).
Pilot runs with select accounts for at least a year before wider rollout.

items.title: Hydrogen land-speed record smashed at 406 MPH
points: Andy Green, 64, drove the JCB Hydromax to 406.320 MPH, more than doubling BMW H2R's 185.5 MPH hydrogen-combustion record from 2004.
The vehicle went from 50 to 400 MPH in 72 seconds.

items.title: US humanoid robotics faces Chinese supply-chain dominance
points: China holds near-total control of robotics component supply chains and has poured billions in state funding into the sector.
Building Chinese-parts-free robots is currently impractical; US makers need major financial and policy support.

items.title: Vercel Labs' Foreman automates the dev pipeline with AI agents
points: Pipeline of agents: Classifier triages tasks, Analyst plans, Implementer executes in a sandbox, Reviewer validates against the actual code diff.
Pulls tasks from GitHub and Linear and outputs a reviewed draft pull request for human approval and merge.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash with 50% price cut
points: Temporarily halved API prices while improving coding accuracy and tool-calling for agents; billed as Google's most capable coding model for multi-step tasks.
Now powers the Gemini Spark personal AI agent.

items.title: OpenAI researcher: technical interviews are obsolete
points: Phil Chen argues LeetCode and system-design interviews test tool use that agents now automate, not job performance.
Value shifts to judgment: choosing the right problems and defining ambitious work AI can't do alone.
Advice: build reputation with your team, join frontier companies on the hardest problems, and think like a researcher who debugs and innovates.

items.title: Workflow claims 95% token-cost reduction for Claude and Codex
points: Viral technique offloads repetitive, context-heavy grunt work to local models, cutting bills for high-volume tasks.
A DeepLearning.ai tutorial covers hybrid cloud/local routing for privacy and lower latency.
Tool 'CodeBurn' audits AI coding spend across models and agents, flags waste, auto-fixes and reports savings.

items.title: Google wearables estimate insulin resistance with no blood draw
points: Combines heart-rate patterns, sleep, activity and skin temperature to estimate insulin-resistance changes (how well the body responds to insulin) without a glucose sensor.
Launches fall 2026 on Pixel Watch 3, 4, 5 and the $99 screenless Fitbit Air, spanning devices from $99 to $1,899.
Marketed as an early-warning wellness signal, explicitly not a medical diagnosis or replacement for clinical glucose monitoring.
Part of a Health Guardian suite adding blood-pressure insights and sleep-breathing and breathing-emergency detection.

items.title: Flock Safety tightens license-plate camera data rules after abuse report
points: Network logs ~20 billion license-plate scans monthly; a report found it used in 46 cases of officers accused of abusing access to track people.
Default retention drops from 30 days to 7, with mandatory Audit Assistance flagging abnormal searches by year-end and city-level query controls.
No warrant requirement added; civil-liberties groups call the changes a 'thinly veiled PR attempt.'

items.title: Pixel 11 line becomes a Gemini-first device
points: Pixel 11 $899 (256GB), Pro $1,099, Pro XL $1,299, Pro Fold $1,899; ships August 20 with Tensor G6, Qi2.2 charging and a 48MP main camera with 56% better low-light sensitivity.
Gemini handles multistep tasks across 40+ apps, pulls context from chats and bookings, and suggests actions in Calendar and Maps.
HiLight RGB ring in the Pro camera bar colors favorite callers and pulses while Gemini listens; $29 Pixel Tag tracker ships November 11 using 1B+ Android devices as its location network.
Gives Google a first-mover edge on native Gemini hardware as Apple prepares to run Google models inside Siri.

items.title: Joby Aviation buys defense contractor Resonant Sciences for $500M
points: ~$450M cash plus $50M stock for the 250-person Dayton, Ohio firm; over 90% of staff hold security clearances, closing expected H1 2027.
Resonant brings $100M+ annual revenue and is operationally profitable; Joby's Q2 revenue was $38.6M, mostly from its Blade helicopter unit ($36.2M).
New division absorbs Joby's turbine-electric, hydrogen-electric and defense-autonomy programs as the company expects to burn $385M-$415M in H2 2026.

items.title: Quick hits: Databricks, perovskite solar, maglev
points: Databricks closed a $5B round at a $190B valuation.
Tandem PV began selling 30.4%-efficient perovskite solar panels (a newer thin-film solar material).
A Chinese maglev train reached 800 km/h in 5.3 seconds.

items.title: Trump imposes 100% tariff on large imported drones
points: 100% tariff on large imported drones and 25% on smaller ones, primarily aimed at Chinese maker DJI while favoring allied nations.
U.S. drone stocks jumped on the news.

items.title: Apple proposes 15% commission on off-App-Store purchases
points: Apple asked the court to permit 15% on outside-app purchases, down from the 27% it charges despite an existing injunction in the Epic Games case.
The Supreme Court refused to pause proceedings over whether Apple violated that injunction; Apple's brief is due September 14.
Apple cited Google Play's rates (20% standard, 15% program, 10% subscription) as precedent Epic already accepted.

items.title: Judge orders Google to drop Android app-store install friction
points: Judge James Donato gave Google seven days to remove unnecessary warning screens and confirmation steps that slow rival app store installs.
Epic showed users had to tap 'view' before 'install' appeared; the judge rejected Google's security justification.
Builds on a jury finding that Google held an illegal monopoly over Android app distribution.

items.title: Apple builds custom AI model with Alibaba for China
points: First time Apple built its own large language model instead of licensing Google's Gemini or ChatGPT, using Alibaba's Qwen model plus Baidu tech.
Apple Intelligence is expected in China within months, likely with iOS 27, across iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro.
China's Cyberspace Administration registered the service, making Apple the only Western firm cleared to offer its own AI model there.

items.title: WhatsApp tests on-device scam detection
points: AI models run entirely on the phone to flag suspicious messages from non-contacts, with no message content leaving the device.
Trained on user-reported scam patterns; users can block, report, mark as trusted, or continue the chat.
Meta plans to publish model weights publicly so researchers can verify the models only detect scams.

sections.title: 1. Career Advice for Engineers in the AI Era
points: Standard coding interviews (LeetCode, system design) are outdated—they test tool use, not job performance, since agents now automate those skills.
Real value shifts to judgment: picking the right problems to solve and defining ambitious work that AI can't yet automate alone.

Stay valuable by building reputation with your team, recognizing impact, joining frontier companies tackling the hardest versions of problems, and thinking like a researcher who debugs and innovates rather than executes.
Focus your energy on time, relationships, and what scales—shipping great code matters less than ensuring the right people know about your impact.

sections.title: 2. New AI Models and Pricing Shifts
points: Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash temporarily halved API prices while improving coding accuracy and tool-calling for agents; it now powers Gemini Spark personal AI agent.
Z.ai's GLM 5.3 achieves competitive performance on Terminal Bench 2.1 through post-training scaling alone (same 743B base as v5.2), available now via API with full weights shipping in ~2 weeks.
DeepSeek released open-source Harness v0.1 (coding framework alternative to paid solutions) and V4-Pro optimized for agents, but users face imminent API price increases for existing V4 access.

sections.title: 3. Token Cost Optimization and Local AI Workflows
points: Trending technique reduces token spending by 95% for Claude and Codex by offloading repetitive context work to local processing, cutting bills dramatically for high-volume tasks.

DeepLearning.ai tutorial covers building tailored AI workflows that switch between cloud and local models, routing specialized tasks to optimized agents while maintaining privacy and reducing latency.
Tool 'CodeBurn' now tracks exactly where AI coding budget goes, flags waste, auto-fixes, and shows savings—enabling teams to audit spend across multiple models and agents in one dashboard.

Flock Safety tightens data practices after report found its camera network used in 46 abuse cases, cutting default retention from 30 to 7 days but stopping short of warrant requirements.
Google turns Pixel phones into Gemini-first devices with new multitask AI capabilities, $29 Pixel Tag tracker, and upgraded cameras launching August 20.

sections.title: Google Wearables Track Insulin Resistance Without Sensors
points: System combines heart-rate patterns, sleep, activity, and skin temperature signals to estimate insulin-resistance changes—no blood glucose reading or sensor required.
Feature launches fall 2026 on Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 plus Fitbit Air, making metabolic monitoring available from $99 screenless band up to premium smartwatches.
Google positions tool as early-warning wellness signal, not medical diagnosis or treatment device, explicitly disclaiming use for replacing clinical glucose monitoring.
Part of broader Health Guardian suite adding blood-pressure insights, sleep-breathing detection, and breathing-emergency detection across Google's wearable ecosystem.

sections.title: Flock Safety Responds to Privacy Backlash
points: Network records ~20 billion license-plate scans monthly; report found system used in 46 cases of police officers accused of abusing access to track individuals.
New safeguards: 7-day default retention (down from 30), mandatory Audit Assistance by year-end flagging abnormal searches, and city-level controls over who can query camera data.
Warrant requirement not imposed; police still decide whom to search, and civil liberties groups call changes a 'thinly veiled PR attempt' rather than structural reform.
Scale remains critical: at 20B monthly scans, defaults become de facto privacy policy regardless of opt-in mechanisms.

HiLight (RGB LED ring in Pro camera bar) colors incoming calls from favorites and pulses while Gemini listens; $29 Pixel Tag tracker ships November 11 tapping 1B+ Android devices for location network.
Move gives Google first-mover advantage defining Gemini on native hardware while Apple prepares to run Google models inside Siri, shifting AI rivalry beyond screens.

New division absorbs Joby's turbine-electric, hydrogen-electric, and defense-autonomy programs; Joby expects to burn $385M–$415M cash in H2 2026, making profitable operations critical.
Strategy shifts Joby from loss-making startup to hybrid holding: near-term revenue from defense contracts while air-taxi certification and commercialization remains multi-year bet.

issues.subject: ☕️ Trump slaps 100% tariff on imported drones

headlines: Trump imposes 100% tariff on large imported drones and 25% on smaller ones, primarily targeting Chinese manufacturer DJI while favoring allied nations, causing U.S. drone stocks to jump.
Apple proposes 15% commission on off-store app purchases in Epic Games dispute, compared to Google Play's 20% standard rate and risking Supreme Court contempt charges.
Federal judge orders Google to remove extra warning screens blocking rival Android app store installations within one week, building on Epic's antitrust victory.
Apple built a custom AI model with Alibaba for China users, becoming the only Western firm cleared by Beijing to offer its own AI in the country.
Chinese startup Zhipu claims its GLM-5.3 coding model beats OpenAI on coding benchmarks and found 2,436 software vulnerabilities across decades-old projects.

sections.title: Apple's App Store Commission Battle
points: Apple asked the court to allow 15% commission on purchases outside the App Store, compared to the 27% it currently charges despite a judge's injunction.
Supreme Court refused to pause proceedings while deciding if Apple violated the earlier injunction, forcing Apple to file its Supreme Court brief by September 14.
Apple cited Google Play's rates (20% standard, 15% program, 10% subscription) as market precedent, noting Epic agreed to those exact Google rates.

sections.title: Google's Android Monopoly Enforcement
points: Judge James Donato ordered Google to strip unnecessary warning screens and confirmation steps that artificially slow rival app store installations within seven days.
Epic demonstrated users faced obstruction like needing to tap 'view' before 'install' appeared—barriers the judge called unacceptable anticompetitive friction.
Google claimed the barriers exist for user security, but the judge rejected that defense, building on a jury finding that Google held illegal monopoly control over Android app distribution.

sections.title: Apple and China's AI Partnership
points: Apple partnered with Alibaba to deploy a custom large language model in China, marking the first time the company built its own AI rather than licensing Google's Gemini or ChatGPT.
Apple Intelligence is expected to arrive in China within months, likely with iOS 27, and will work on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro using Alibaba's Qwen model plus Baidu technology.
China's Cyberspace Administration registered Apple's generative AI service last month—a regulatory approval that makes Apple the only Western firm cleared to offer its own AI model in China.

sections.title: WhatsApp's On-Device Scam Detection
points: WhatsApp is testing a Scam Detection feature using AI models that run entirely on users' phones to flag suspicious messages from non-contacts, with no message content leaving the device.
The tool, trained on user-reported scam patterns, displays a private warning and lets people block, report, mark as trusted, or continue conversations.
Meta plans to publish model weights and versions publicly so security researchers can verify the models only detect scams and don't monitor message content.
